about: The AI settings a site names itself, as both backends must read them: AI_FEATURES, AI_DAILY_LIMIT, AI_DAILY_LIMITS and AI_MODELS in .env (Node, loadAiSettings in server/config.ts), 'features', 'dailyLimit', 'dailyLimits' and 'models' in config.php's ai block (PHP, AiConfig). Replayed by tests/unit/ai-config.test.ts and php/tests/ConfigTest.php. `env` is the variable's value (null: not set), `php` the key's value; a row without one of them is the other backend's alone. A refusal names the setting and never repeats its value. The default and the most a site may set are AI_DAILY_LIMIT and AI_DAILY_LIMIT_MAX in src/shared/ai.ts: both tests hold these rows to them. A `dailyLimits` row may set the site's own number beside the pairs (`site`: AI_DAILY_LIMIT, 'dailyLimit'); an accepted one says which features end up with a number of their own (`limits`) and what every other feature gets (`others`), so a new feature changes no row. A `models` row (AI_MODELS, 'models') reads the same way: `site` is the site's own model (AI_MODEL, 'model'), `models` the features that end up with a model of their own, and every other feature gets the site's, or the provider's default. The first rows of `models` (`defaults`) say what every feature runs on with a provider named, as literal model names: the picture read has a default of its own on each real provider, its middle model (AI_FEATURE_DEFAULT_MODEL; the owner's answer, 2026-10-06, after the fast models wrote a wrong time off a handwritten board). That default wins over the site's own model, which is the flyer's and the share text's, and only the read's own pair changes it. Those rows name every feature, so a new feature adds to them.
